sources.citation: Rajakrishna, M. 2022. A Study on the Morphosyntax of Compound Verbs in Kolami. PhD thesis, Dept. of Dravidian and Computational Linguistics, Dravidian University, Kuppam (supervisor P. Sreekumar). Data from Adilabad Kolami (Utnoor, Jainoor, Tiryani, Kerimeri, Sirpur). Shodhganga 10603/561465; title, prelims, ch. 1, ch. 2, bibliography read.
sources.note: sec. 1.10 'Phonological structure of Kolami' (pp. 16-17) gives only vowel and consonant charts ('five vowels in Kolami with length to each.. Length occurs in the initial and medial positions'); no suprasegmentals anywhere; silent on stress. Bibliography identifies Subrahmanyam 2010 'Kolavagotti (Kolami of Adilabad)' BDCRI 70: 173-248 and Thomasaiah 1986 as the descriptions of this variety.

sources.citation: Emeneau, M. B. 1955 [2nd ed. 1961, Annamalai University reprint]. Kolami, a Dravidian Language (University of California Publications in Linguistics 12). Berkeley / Annamalainagar. xvi+302 pp. Read ch. I pp. 1-5, ch. II pp. 6-9, ch. IX 'Characteristics of the dialect in SR (with a few notes on the Kinwat and Pandharkavra dialects)' pp. 130-140 (scanned of the Tamil Digital Library scan).
sources.note: p. 8 sec. 2.10 'Accent. The first syllable of a word has a stress accent of medium intensity..' -- but this is the WARDHA dialect (Northwestern Kolami, nort2699). For the Adilabad dialect (SR = Setumadhava Rao 1950, i.e. sout1549 Utnur/Asifabad) p. 130 sec. 9.1: 'No list of phonemes or of phonetic entities is given by SR. I can only attempt to evaluate his transcriptions by comparison with what I give for W.'; ch. IX treats vowel length, d/r, c~ts/s, plurals, numerals only; nothing on accent for SR or Kinwat; Naiki of Chanda not described. Silent for sout1549.
sources.venue: University of California Publications in Linguistics 12

sources.citation: Gurov, N. V. 2013. Dravidijskie jazyki [Дравидийские языки; 'The Dravidian languages']. In A. M. Dubjanskij, E. B. Markus, N. V. Gurov & A. A. Kibrik (eds.), Jazyki mira: Dravidijskie jazyki, 17-46. Moskva: Academia. ISBN 978-5-87444-369-6.
sources.note: Describes another variety (Glottolog drav1251). Explicit family-level statement, p. 28: Dravidian languages have no tones (though intonation contours of long and short vowels are melodically coloured differently); stress gravitates to an initial long syllable, in words of short CV syllables as a rule on the first syllable; many languages also have phrase stress on the utterance-final syllable.

tone.quote: П р о с о д и я Д.я. может быть описана лишь в самых общих чертах. В Д.я. отсутствуют тоны (хотя интонационные контуры долгих и кратких гласных мелодически окрашены по-разному). Ударение тяготеет к начальному долгому слогу. В словах, состоящих из кратких слогов типа CV, ударение, как правило, на первом слоге. Во многих языках помимо силового отмечается также фразовое ударение, фиксирующееся на финальном слоге высказывания.
tone.locator: p. 28, section 'Просодия' of the family chapter 'Дравидийские языки'
tone.translation: The prosody of the Dravidian languages can be described only in the most general terms. In the Dravidian languages tones are absent (although the intonation contours of long and short vowels are melodically coloured differently). Stress gravitates toward an initial long syllable. In words consisting of short syllables of the type CV, stress is as a rule on the first syllable. In many languages, besides dynamic stress, phrasal stress fixed on the final syllable of the utterance is also noted.
tone.summary: Family-level: no tones in Dravidian; stress tends to the initial (long) syllable; utterance-final phrasal prominence in many languages.
tone.says: Explicit family-level statement, p. 28: Dravidian languages have no tones (though intonation contours of long and short vowels are melodically coloured differently); stress gravitates to an initial long syllable, in words of short CV syllables as a rule on the first syllable; many languages also have phrase stress on the utterance-final syllable.
